answer:
You can re-run only the errored test cases in two ways.

**Option 1: Retry errors from the latest eval.** Run:

```sh
promptfoo eval --retry-errors
```

"The retry errors feature automatically finds ERROR results from the latest eval and re-runs only those test cases. This is useful when evals fail due to temporary network issues, rate limits, or API errors." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]

**Option 2: Retry errors from a specific eval.** Pass the eval ID:

```sh
promptfoo retry eval-abc123
```

"Retry all ERROR results from a specific eval. This command finds test cases that resulted in errors (e.g., from network issues, rate limits, or API failures) and re-runs only those test cases. The results are updated in place in the original eval." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]

Some notes:

- If the retry fails, your original errors are kept. "If the retry fails, your original ERROR results are preserved." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md] You can run the command again.
- `--retry-errors` cannot be combined with `--resume` or `--no-write`. [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]
- Use `promptfoo retry` when you want to fix errors in an existing eval without creating a duplicate. "Use `retry` when you want to fix errors in an existing eval without creating duplicates." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]
